// Win32/COM surface generated by CsWin32 (see docs/adr/0005-cswin32-for-wasapi-interop.md).
// Each entry below is required by a specific part of docs/design.md; keep the
// annotations current so an unused entry is obvious during review.

// --- MuteActuator (design.md 7.3) ---
IMMDeviceEnumerator
IMMDevice
IMMNotificationClient
IAudioEndpointVolume
MMDeviceEnumerator
EDataFlow
ERole
DEVICE_STATE
// DEVICE_STATE matters more than it looks. 7.3 says an entry whose endpoint is *gone* is
// cleared without an error, and a retained-but-unplugged headset is NOT gone - clearing its
// entry is what strands it across manual rows D1 and D2. Enumerating with UNPLUGGED and
// NOTPRESENT included is how the two cases stay distinguishable.

// --- MicWatcher (design.md 7.2) ---
IAudioSessionManager2
IAudioSessionEnumerator
IAudioSessionControl2
AudioSessionState

// --- HotkeyListener (design.md 7.4) ---
RegisterHotKey
UnregisterHotKey
HOT_KEY_MODIFIERS

// --- HostWindow (design.md 7.1 departure, work item 6) ---
// The host marshals every arbitration mutation onto its message-only window's thread, so it
// needs to wake that thread from the socket receive thread and the cadence timer.
// Control.BeginInvoke is not available: a message-only NativeWindow is deliberately not a
// WinForms Control, because a Control is a real top-level window and the host is headless
// until work item 9 adds the tray.
PostMessage

// Rejoin quarantine (design.md 7.6) needs network-change notifications to restart the
// window. That comes from System.Net.NetworkInformation.NetworkChange in the BCL, not
// from interop, so there is deliberately no entry for NotifyAddrChange here.

// --- RestoreCommand (design.md 7.3, work item 7) ---
// SoloSpeaker.exe is a WinExe, so it has no console and an invoking shell sees nothing at
// all. uninstall.ps1 reads both the message and the exit code before deciding whether to
// delete the binary and the ledger, so --restore has to be able to speak.
AttachConsole
ATTACH_PARENT_PROCESS

// --- FileStore durability (design.md 7.3, work item 7) ---
// Flushing the file buys ordering; the rename itself is logged lazily by NTFS, so the
// directory entry needs its own flush. System.IO cannot open a directory handle, which is
// why this is interop rather than a FileStream.
FlushFileBuffers
CreateFile
